findings.title: OpenAI introduces GPT-6 Cyber via X
findings.summary_md: OpenAI announced GPT-6 Cyber as a major advance in security research that pairs stronger capabilities with better model alignment. The post states the model powered the Linux kernel research announced the previous day and was used to find 81 previously unknown high-severity Firefox vulnerabilities. Access is limited to approved Daybreak Red customers.

findings.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Cyber, and promises this one stays within 'rules of engagement'
findings.summary_md: OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber, a cybersecurity-tuned model rated Critical under its Preparedness Framework, available initially through the API and Codex to approved Daybreak Red customers. Its researchers used it to find 81 previously unknown high-severity vulnerabilities in Firefox and to develop working exploits for 948 Linux kernel privilege-escalation bugs. The model scored 48.5 percent on ExploitGym versus 32.1 percent for GPT-5.6 Cyber and avoided out-of-scope exploitation in 99.93 percent of cases.

findings.title: OpenAI debuts GPT-6 Cyber, touting better performance and safety guardrails
findings.summary_md: OpenAI announced a cybersecurity-focused model citing internal benchmark improvements in vulnerability discovery, patch development, and adherence to safety guardrails. Preview results included at least 81 novel Firefox vulnerabilities, exploits for 948 Linux kernel bugs, and a validated critical remote-code-execution flaw in Brotli. The model rolls out first to a limited set of Daybreak Red customers, with safeguards such as identity checks and frequent high-risk behavior check-ins.

findings.title: OpenAI says GPT-6 Cyber is better at finding vulnerabilities without going out of bounds
findings.summary_md: OpenAI launched GPT-6 Cyber, saying it goes out of bounds less than one percent of the time and scored 48.5 percent on ExploitGym. The model is rolling out to select Daybreak Red customers for authorized defensive cybersecurity work, with expanded access planned in coming weeks. OpenAI also noted stronger safeguards against high-risk activity including attacks on critical infrastructure.

findings.title: OpenAI AI pipeline generates 948 Linux root escalation exploits
findings.summary_md: An OpenAI autonomous pipeline identified and analyzed 2,308 candidate Linux kernel findings, dynamically reproduced 1,724 vulnerabilities, and produced 948 local privilege escalation exploits. The campaign cost about $1,213,430 in API credits and built on an earlier July 2026 run that exploited 166 vulnerabilities. OpenAI reported 304 critical findings to Linux maintainers with candidate patches.

findings.title: AI agents got root on Linux via 948 kernel flaws in OpenAI research
findings.summary_md: An unreleased OpenAI cyber model found and exploited 948 distinct Linux kernel privilege escalation bugs for about $1.2 million. OpenAI counted 948 unique vulnerabilities and wrote 948 patches, with human researchers reviewing results before reporting to kernel maintainers. The findings were produced using a variant of the company's frontier cyber model.

findings.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber, finds 81 high-severity Firefox flaws and 948 Linux exploits
findings.summary_md: OpenAI launched GPT-6 Cyber, a security-focused AI model that found 81 new high-severity Firefox flaws and built working exploits for 948 Linux kernel bugs. The company disclosed 304 critical findings to Linux maintainers with candidate patches while work on other vulnerabilities continues. Mozilla has begun fixing the Firefox issues.
